title: What Reversals Take Back Out of a Ridgecrest RxSecure Out-of-Pocket Total
content:
What the reversals on the pharmacy record take back out of an out-of-pocket total on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan is read from the number of reversals standing on that record and from the standing of the enrollment. The plan treats 2 or more reversals as a run of reversals.

1. Where the reversals standing on the pharmacy record are 2 or more and the enrollment stands in force, what is taken back out is the whole of what every reversal on the record carries.
2. Where the reversals standing on the pharmacy record are fewer than 2 and the enrollment stands in force, what is taken back out is what the reversals with a fill date in the 3 months up to the handling date carry.
3. Where neither holds, nothing is taken back out for reversals.

| Reversals standing on the pharmacy record | Standing of the enrollment | What is taken back out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 or more | in force | the whole of what every reversal on the record carries |
| fewer than 2 | in force | what the reversals dated in the 3 months up to the handling date carry |
| 2 or more | in its premium grace period, terminated, or any other footing | nothing |
| fewer than 2 | in its premium grace period, terminated, or any other footing | nothing |

A record carrying exactly 2 reversals meets the run of reversals; one carrying a single reversal does not, and only reversals dated inside the 3-month window are then reached.

## Worked on a hypothetical record

Take a record carrying reversals of member payments of 18.00 USD and 9.50 USD, the later of them dated inside the 3 months up to the handling date and the earlier outside it.

- With the enrollment in force and both reversals standing: 27.50 USD is taken back out.
- With the enrollment in force and only the later reversal standing: 9.50 USD is taken back out, being what the reversals inside the 3-month window carry.
- With the enrollment in its premium grace period: nothing is taken back out, however many reversals stand on the record.
